risks.note: The industry deals with high pressures, fast-moving components and heavy machinery; accidents involving hydraulic systems can result in severe injuries or fatalities if not properly managed, and fluid leaks, explosions and unexpected movements of components all pose significant safety risks.

Hydraulic systems use fluids to transmit power; leaks can cause fluid contamination and spillage with negative environmental consequences, and hydraulic fluids can be harmful to the environment and water sources if not handled and disposed of properly.
Hydraulic systems require regular maintenance and inspection; neglect can lead to equipment failures, unexpected downtime and safety hazards.
Pumps, valves and hoses wear over time under high pressures and forces, leading to inefficiencies, reduced performance and increased risk of system failure.

Hydraulic systems have historically been criticised for energy inefficiency (fluid leaks, internal friction, pressure losses); as environmental concerns and energy costs rise, demand shifts toward more energy-efficient hydraulic solutions, pressuring legacy product lines.
Prevailing global uncertainty and the continuous reorganisation of supply chains, both in India and other countries, has the potential to impact the Company's revenues.

Technologies are ever evolving, creating risk of changing preferences in pumping technologies, novel technologies displacing existing ones, and increasing competition for existing markets especially from copycat products.

MD&A and the Board's Report refer to 'the manufacturing unit' in the singular and state there was no change in the nature of business; the Company operates in a single niche hydraulics business, so operational disruption at the unit or a downturn in hydraulics is not diversified away. All properties and insurable interests including building, plant and machinery and stocks are stated to be fully insured.
